subject: Regional entitlements, billing currency, and product page copy for upcoming AWS listing
messages:
From: Amit Rao <amit.rao@amazon.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: AWS Marketplace Catalog Team <aws-marketplace-catalog@amazon.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: AWS listing: regional availability + billing currency questions

Hi Sofia / Kimberly,

Thanks again for walking through the BluePeak offer details with the marketplace onboarding team yesterday. A couple items popped up while cataloging the listing that I wanted to confirm before we push the draft product page live: 

1) Regional entitlement scope: BluePeak wants the product visible in all commercial regions, but they're also asking to enable Private Offers in EU regions. Is Redwood able to support Private Offer flows for EU customers for this SKU? If there are any additional contract or entitlement notes we should surface on the page, send them over.

2) Billing currency: catalog metadata needs a primary settlement currency. BluePeak sells globally but prefers to invoice in EUR to a subset of customers—do you want us to list USD only, or mark multi-currency support with a footnote? If the platform itself only reports USD usage to AWS (and you handle customer invoicing separately), we should capture that precisely in the listing copy.

3) Product page microcopy: We captured a short hero blurb during the call; attaching a regional matrix for your review. Any suggested changes to the entitlement language (trial, private offer, buyer regions) would help us avoid later delistings.

Attaching: aws_region_matrix.xlsx

Appreciate a quick confirmation ideally by Monday so catalog can proceed.

Best,
Amit
Marketplace Partner Manager, AWS

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Amit Rao <amit.rao@amazon.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS listing: regional availability + billing currency questions

Hi Amit — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and a few asks below. Copying Kim and Marissa for procurement/ops input.

Regional entitlement / Private Offer in EU:
- Redwood supports Private Offers in EU regions when the customer signs a Private Offer contract. There are two caveats: (1) for EU-based procurement we require the Private Offer to reference our EU legal entity, and (2) some regions require the SKU to be flagged as "EU-only private offers" in catalog metadata to avoid cross-region provisioning issues.
- Action: can you flag specifically which EU regions BluePeak expects to sell into (e.g., eu-west-1, eu-central-1)? I've attached the regional-entitlements-checklist.pdf with the fields we need for EU Private Offers.

Billing currency:
- Platform settlement to AWS is USD by default for Redwood's hosted offers. We can surface "Customer invoices may be issued in EUR for EU customers" as a footnote on the product page, but we need Marissa to confirm that our billing ops can support sending EUR invoices for this account without changing settlement reporting to AWS.

Product page copy suggestions (high level):
- Hero one-liner: "Redwood Inference — predictable, production-grade LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments." (shorten to fit hero line)
- Entitlement bullet: "Available in US and EU commercial regions. Private Offers supported in EU regions (requires separate Private Offer contract)."
- Billing footnote (if ops confirms): "Invoices to EU customers may be issued in EUR; AWS settlement remains in USD."

Kim / Marissa — can you confirm the EUR invoicing capability and any legal clauses we should include for Private Offers in EU? Also please flag whether the product page should show "EU: Private Offer only" under the region availability table or leave it implicit.

Thanks,
Sofia
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference

On Fri, Jun 29, 2028 at 2:12 PM Amit Rao <amit.rao@amazon.com> wrote:
> (original message and attachment omitted)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Jul 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS listing: regional availability + billing currency questions

Sofia / Marissa — quick internal note and suggested copy snippets.

Operational answers:
- EUR invoicing: Finance can generate EUR invoices to EU customers, but those invoices are managed outside AWS settlement. We need a one-time onboarding change for BluePeak (to map their billing profile to our EU invoicing flow). That on-boarding typically takes 7-10 business days and requires a signed billing addendum.
- Private Offer flags: For EU Private Offers, we should tag the SKU as "EU-PrivateOffersEnabled" in the catalog metadata. This prevents the offer from being surfaced as a public listing in regions where we don't want Private Offers visible. That tag is safe and commonly used.

Suggested product page copy (to give catalog a ready-to-paste):
Hero (short): "High-performance LLM inference across cloud and private deployments — optimized for latency, reliability, and unit cost."
Availability (table/bullet): "Available: US commercial regions. EU commercial regions: listing visible; Private Offers supported for EU buyers (requires separate Private Offer contract)."
Billing footnote (compact): "Note: AWS settlement is processed in USD. Redwood may issue customer invoices in EUR for EU buyers upon request (requires billing onboarding)."

Attachments: pricing-footnotes.docx (contains the exact billing language we've used for previous EU private offers).

Next steps:
1) Sofia — confirm which EU regions Amit / BluePeak need.
2) Marissa — initiate billing onboarding with Finance if BluePeak needs EUR invoicing. I'll draft the billing addendum template when you confirm.

-Kim
Director, Go-to-Market Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Amit Rao <amit.rao@amazon.com>, Eva <eva@bluepeak.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Jul 2028 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS listing: regional availability + billing currency questions

Hi Amit / Eva — thanks for the patience while we pulled internal ops and legal in. Quick summary and recommended copy for the catalog team: 

Decisions / confirmations:
- Regions: BluePeak confirmed target EU regions: eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 (see HubSpot note: https://hubspot.com/deals/MWP-7832). Please enable listing visibility in those regions.
- Private Offers: Supported in the EU regions listed above. Catalog should tag the SKU as "EU-PrivateOffersEnabled" to prevent public exposure outside intended regions.
- Billing: AWS settlement will remain USD. Redwood will invoice EU buyers in EUR upon request after completing a one-time billing onboarding (7-10 business days) and a signed billing addendum.

Catalog copy (please use the lines below on the product page):
Hero: "High-performance LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — optimized for latency, reliability, and cost."
Availability bullet: "Available in US commercial regions. EU commercial regions (eu-west-1, eu-central-1): listing visible; Private Offers supported in EU regions (requires separate Private Offer contract)."
Billing footnote: "Note: AWS settlement is processed in USD. Redwood may issue customer invoices in EUR for EU buyers upon request (requires billing onboarding)."

Attachments: regional-entitlements-checklist.pdf, pricing-footnotes.docx (attached for catalog/legal reference).

Next steps:
- Amit / Catalog: apply the SKU tag and update the marketplace record. Let me know if you need the signed billing addendum template — Kim will draft it after Marissa confirms onboarding.
- Eva / BluePeak: confirm acceptance of the billing onboarding timeline and that eu-west-1 + eu-central-1 are sufficient.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if any of the wording needs tightening for catalog constraints.

Cheers,
Sofia
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
